*** GILT WARNING: CNBC's PREVIOUS CLOSE HAS CHANGED SINCE THIS MORNING ***
At 07:36 BST CNBC gave UK10Y-GB prev close 5.3657%. By this evening it gives 5.4258% and shows the
day as -0.024. The 5.4258 figure does not fit the day's own range: today's open was 5.3954 and the
low was 5.3702, both well below 5.4258. The Friday reference is also backed up elsewhere: TradingEconomics
says 10y gilt yields "eased slightly to 5.35%" on 25 Sep. And today its narrative says "UK 10-year gilt
yields rose to 5.4%, their highest level in nearly two decades, as investors priced in a more
hawkish Bank of England policy stance... BoE Deputy Governor Dave Ramsden said Monday he would support
rate hikes if 'upside pressures' on inflation persist." TradingEconomics is not an approved outlet,
so it is used as a cross-check only. Published change is therefore measured against the morning's
sourced prev close: 5.4017-5.3657 = +0.036, so +0.04. That makes it the morning's own basis carried
forward. If the desk prefers CNBC's literal field, it is -0.02. DO NOT describe gilts as falling today.
(UK2Y-GB shows the same pattern: prev 4.9244 vs open 4.8716. CNBC's live blog says "The U.K.'s
2-year yield rose 5 basis points".) UK30Y-GB 5.8928%.

MOVES SINCE THIS MORNING'S EDITION:
- FTSE: opened flat, hit 10,758.74 (Investing.com/Reuters had it +0.58% at 0829 GMT), then faded all
  afternoon to close on its low, -0.10%. Housebuilders surged; miners and precious-metal miners slumped.

- Gold: fell from -2.56% this morning to -3.64%. Seven-week low, the lowest since 5 August (Reuters).
- Sterling: moved from -0.11% this morning to +0.12%. Euro-sterling -0.27%.
